info.name: GameBuddy Backend
info.description:
Every HTTP endpoint the monolith exposes, generated from the controllers.

## Getting started

1. Select the **GameBuddy Local** environment (or set `baseUrl` yourself).
2. Run **Auth > Register**, then **Auth > Send verification code**, then **Auth > Verify** with the code from the email.
3. Run **Auth > Login**. It stores the token automatically — every other request picks it up from collection auth, so you never paste a bearer token by hand.

## Notes

- `POST /auth/register` returns a token, but the account cannot do much until it is verified and has completed `/auth/details`.
- Requests under **Admin** need `ROLE_ADMIN`. Promote an account directly in the database: `UPDATE gamebuddy.gamer SET role = 'ADMIN' WHERE email = '...';`
- Chat messages are sent over **STOMP/WebSocket**, not HTTP, so they are not in this collection. Connect to `{{wsUrl}}` with an `Authorization: Bearer` header on CONNECT and send to `/app/chat`. The HTTP endpoints here read history and report messages.
- There is no endpoint the app can call to claim a purchase. Receipts go to RevenueCat, which verifies them with Apple or Google and posts the outcome to `POST /billing/revenuecat/webhook`. That webhook is the only way an entitlement can be granted, and it is guarded by a shared secret sent in the `Authorization` header (`REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`) — the backend refuses to start without one.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Registration, verification, login and account management.

exec: // Registration returns a token straight away. Stored so the follow-up
// calls work without a manual copy-paste.

request.description: Public. Password must satisfy the policy in `PasswordPolicy` — length plus mixed character classes; a weak one comes back as 147 WEAK_PASSWORD.
Public, and rate limited (3 per 15 minutes per address) so it cannot be used to mail-bomb anyone. Set `isRegister` false for a password reset.
Public, rate limited (10 per 15 minutes). Without that limit the six-digit space is walkable.
Public. An unknown address and a wrong password return the same error on purpose, so this cannot be used to discover which addresses are registered.
Also returns false for a token that was valid but has since been revoked — password change, ban, or account deletion all move `tokensValidFrom` forward.
Onboarding. `age` decides the age band, and a gamer is only ever matched or chatted with inside their own band.
Revokes every token issued before now — the point of changing a password is usually that you think one was stolen. Log in again afterwards.
A paid avatar has to have been bought first; selecting one you do not own is refused.
Crossing the majority line changes which pool you match in, and takes effect immediately on conversations already open.

Claiming a token detaches it from every other account. A token identifies a device, so exactly one account may hold it — otherwise a reinstall or a shared phone sends one person's notifications to another.
Anonymises rather than deletes the row, because posts, comments and messages reference it. The account stops authenticating everywhere immediately.

item.name: Profile
item.description: Profiles, catalogue, cosmetics, badges and friends.

request.description: Returns strictly less than your own profile: no email, no coin balance, no friend list.

exec: // Grab a game id so the onboarding and match requests have one to use.

request.description: Every mission with this gamer's progress. Not a pure read: the server evaluates the missions while answering, so calling this is what turns a finished one into an earned badge.
Credits the reward. Guarded by an optimistic lock, so two concurrent collects cannot pay out twice. Answers with the whole board.
Replaces the whole selection, in order, up to three. An empty array takes everything off.
Frames and banners, split by kind, with the owned and equipped flags for this gamer.
Spends coins. Read-check-write under the gamer's version, so a double tap cannot buy twice.
By kind rather than by id: "take off my frame" does not require knowing what is on.
Requests this gamer sent that nobody has answered. The mirror of /get/requests/friends, which returns the ones received.
Requires an existing mutual match — friendship is the tier above matching, not a parallel one. Expect 155 FRIEND_REQUIRES_MATCH otherwise.
Takes effect everywhere immediately: recommendations, existing matches, and any open conversation.

item.name: Match
item.description: Recommendations, swiping, matches and the daily allowance.

exec: // Keep the first candidate around so accept/decline have a target.

request.description:
Ranked by the model, filtered to your own age band, with everyone you have already decided on excluded and roughly one in ten slots given to a random candidate so newer gamers stay reachable.

Needs the Python model on `PREDICT_SERVICE_URL`; without it expect 123 RECOMMENDER_SERVICE_ERROR.

Costs a swipe and a like. On the free tier expect 158 ACCEPT_LIMIT_REACHED once the five daily likes are gone, or 163 SWIPE_LIMIT_REACHED once the fifty swipes are.

When the other side has already accepted you, this is the moment the match happens and both are notified.
Costs a swipe but not a like, so declining all day never uses up your likes.
Mutual only. These are the people you can chat with.
The count is always returned. The identities need Gold — on the free tier `locked` is true and `likedYou` is empty.
Swipes and likes remaining, and when they reset. `remainingAccepts` is never larger than `remainingSwipes`: three swipes cannot buy four likes.

item.name: Chat
item.description: Reading history and reporting. Sending is over STOMP — see the collection description.

request.description: Oldest first, decrypted on the way out. Opening a conversation also moves your read watermark, so the unread count on the inbox drops.
One row per conversation with the latest message and an unread count, newest activity first. Conversations with no messages yet are skipped rather than shown empty.
Only the recipient may report, and only inside a conversation they are part of. The text is kept — a moderator has to be able to read what was said.
Ordered and paged in the database, not in memory.
The creator becomes owner and first member.
An owner may leave; ownership passes to the longest-standing member, or the community is removed if nobody is left.
Owner only. Takes its posts and comments with it.
Reporting the same thing twice returns 157 ALREADY_REPORTED.
Reports a gamer rather than something they wrote. Lands in the same queue as posts and comments; refused with 157 on a second attempt against the same person.

The tier actually in force, after checking the expiry — a lapsed subscription reads as BASIC without anything having to write it back. The entitlements come with it so the client does not hard-code what a tier means.

header.description: The shared secret, sent verbatim. Not a bearer token.

request.description:
How an entitlement is granted. RevenueCat has already verified the purchase with the store; this only maps it onto an account.

`app_user_id` must be our `gamer.user_id` — the app sets it via `Purchases.logIn(userId)`. An anonymous id (`$RCAnonymousID:...`) is refused, because there is no account to grant to.

Products: `gamebuddy.gold.weekly`, `gamebuddy.gold.monthly`, `gamebuddy.gold.yearly`, `gamebuddy.coins.500`, `gamebuddy.coins.1200`, `gamebuddy.coins.3000`.

Event types that grant: INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, UNCANCELLATION, PRODUCT_CHANGE, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE. EXPIRATION revokes. CANCELLATION does NOT revoke unless `cancel_reason` is CUSTOMER_SUPPORT (a refund) — an ordinary cancellation only turns off auto-renew, and the subscriber keeps what they paid for until EXPIRATION.

Replaying the same `transaction_id` grants nothing and still answers 200: RevenueCat retries until it gets a 2xx, so duplicates are normal. Anything unrecognised is logged and accepted rather than rejected, because a webhook that keeps failing gets disabled.
Your own history only. There is no send endpoint any more — modules publish an event internally instead of POSTing to each other.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Everything here needs ROLE_ADMIN. Promote an account in the database first.

request.description: Also revokes their tokens, so the ban takes effect on the next request rather than whenever their token happens to expire.

The only place plaintext leaves a conversation. Message bodies are encrypted at rest and normally only decrypted for the two participants; here they are decrypted for a moderator, and every call is logged with the moderator's id.
Marks the report reviewed. Does not delete the message — dismissing a report and removing content are different decisions.
Public, because probes have no credentials. `/actuator/health/liveness` and `/readiness` are what a container orchestrator should watch.
